questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed twice. What is the probability of getting exactly one head?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Sample space for 2 tosses: {HH, HT, TH, TT} — 4 outcomes. Exactly 1 head: {HT, TH} — 2 favourable. P = 2/4 = 1/2. Trap: 1/4 = probability of exactly 2 heads (HH only); 3/4 = probability of at least one head; 1 = certainty (always getting a head is impossible in 2 fair tosses).

questions.stem: A card is drawn at random from a standard deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of drawing a red face card?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Face cards = J, Q, K (3 per suit). Red face cards = Jacks, Queens, Kings of Hearts and Diamonds = 3×2 = 6 cards. P = 6/52 = 3/26. Trap: 6/52 is the same as 3/26 but unsimplified; 1/4 = 13/52 (red cards only, not just face); 3/52 uses 3 face cards (one colour only — forgets both red suits).

questions.stem: A bag contains 3 red and 5 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total balls = 3+5 = 8. Red balls = 3. P(red) = 3/8. Trap: 5/8 = P(blue) = complement; 3/5 uses only red vs blue, ignoring total; 1/4 = wrong computation.

questions.stem: Two dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability of getting a sum of 7?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total outcomes = 6×6 = 36. Pairs summing to 7: (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1) = 6 pairs. P = 6/36 = 1/6. Trap: 7/36 = incorrect count (7 is the sum, not the number of favourable outcomes); 1/12 = 3/36 (only counts 3 pairs); 1/8 = 4.5/36 (impossible fraction).

questions.stem: From a deck of 52 cards, what is the probability of drawing a King or a Queen?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Kings = 4, Queens = 4. No overlap (a card can't be both a King and a Queen). Favourable = 4+4 = 8. P = 8/52 = 2/13. Trap: 4/52 = 1/13 = P(King only) or P(Queen only); 1/26 = 2/52 = wrong count; 2/13 simplified correctly from 8/52.

questions.stem: A bag has 4 white and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn together. What is the probability that both are white?
questions.explanation: B is correct. ⁴C₂ = 6 (ways to choose 2 white from 4). ¹⁰C₂ = 45 (total ways to choose 2 from 10). P = 6/45 = 2/15. Trap: 4/25 = (4/10)² = incorrect (applies replacement formula to without-replacement problem); 1/5 = 9/45 (wrong numerator); 1/6 = 7.5/45 (impossible).

questions.stem: Shooter A has probability 3/5 of hitting a target, and B has probability 2/3. Both shoot independently. What is the probability that the target is hit?
questions.explanation: C is correct. P(target hit) = 1 − P(both miss). P(A misses) = 1−3/5 = 2/5. P(B misses) = 1−2/3 = 1/3. P(both miss) = (2/5)×(1/3) = 2/15. P(hit) = 1−2/15 = 13/15. Trap: 11/15 = 3/5+2/3−1 (wrong addition formula; P(A or B hit)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A and B hit)=3/5+2/3−2/5×2/3=9/15+10/15−6/15=13/15 ✓ same answer via addition formula); 6/15 = P(both hit) = 3/5×2/3 = 6/15 (not the question asked).

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52. What is the probability that both are Kings?
questions.explanation: B is correct. ⁴C₂ = 6 (ways to choose 2 Kings from 4). ⁵²C₂ = (52×51)/2 = 1326 (total ways). P = 6/1326 = 1/221. Trap: 1/169 = (4/52)² = (1/13)² (applies with-replacement formula wrongly); 4/52 = P(first card is a King, ignores second); 1/52 = wrong denominator concept.

questions.stem: Three unbiased coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: C is correct. P(at least 1H) = 1 − P(no heads) = 1 − P(all tails) = 1 − (1/2)³ = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8. Alternatively: out of 8 outcomes, only TTT has no head → 7 favourable. Trap: 3/4 = P(at least 1H in 2 tosses); 3/8 = P(exactly 1 head in 3 tosses) → ³C₁×(1/2)³ = 3/8.

questions.stem: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. One ball is drawn and found to be red; it is not replaced. What is the probability that the second ball drawn is also red?
questions.explanation: B is correct. After first red ball is removed: 3 red, 6 blue remain → 9 total. P(second red | first red) = 3/9 = 1/3. Trap: 2/5 = 4/10 (initial probability before any drawing; forgets the first red was removed); 4/9 = 4/(9) — wrong numerator (still uses original 4 red count); 3/10 = forgets to reduce denominator.
